trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 3 rows chi(4_1,mu), mu |- 3. RECOMPUTED against parent prop:figure-eight-branching-rule. The table faithfully instantiates the parent formula (mu=[3]: a=1,b=0; mu=[1^3]: a=1,b=0; mu=[2,1]: a=-1,b=-1 => -1-h^2), and I confirmed -1-h^2 IS the exact 2-dim Hoefsmit trace of the parent's braid word sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0^{-1} sigma_1 (sympy, eigenvalues q,-q^{-1}: trace = -q^2+1-q^{-2}). BUT that braid word is not the figure-eight knot -- see notes.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: ANOMALY (structural, parent-level, NOT fixed here). prop:figure-eight-branching-rule defines 4_1 = sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0^{-1} sigma_1, a commutator. Its closure is a 1-component knot with reduced-Burau Alexander polynomial det(I-Burau)(1-t)/(1-t^3) = 1/t ~ 1, i.e. the UNKNOT. The genuine figure-eight braid (sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1})^2 gives -(t^2-3t+1)/t^2 ~ t-3+t^{-1}, the 4_1 polynomial (control: same route reproduces it exactly, and correctly returns 0 for the 2-component closure of sigma_1^3). In [2,1] the true 4_1 character is q^4-2q^2+1-2q^{-2}+q^{-4}, NOT -1-h^2; the two coincide only at q=1 (both -1, the S_3 3-cycle character), so the classical part a_lambda survives while every q-deformation term -f^{lambda/[2,1]}h^2 is computed on the wrong knot. Proposed fix: correct the word to (sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1})^2 in figure-eight-branching-rule.md/.lean and re-derive the h^2 coefficient, or rename the object if the commutator is what is intended.
